title: Mikaeus + Yawgmoth: does the -1/-1 counter annihilate undying's +1/+1 and re-arm the body, and what bounds the loop?

you: Gravecrawler (2/1 printed; 3/2 with Mikaeus's +1/+1; carries ONE +1/+1 counter from a previous undying return, so it is currently 4/3)
Viscera Seer (1/1 printed; 2/2 with Mikaeus's +1/+1; no counters) — already sacrificed to pay the cost of the ability now on the stack

scenario.mana_available: {0} (all four Swamps are tapped and nothing else produces mana)

stack.object: Yawgmoth, Thran Physician's activated ability — 'Pay 1 life, Sacrifice another creature: Put a -1/-1 counter on up to one target creature and draw a card.' Both costs already paid: 1 life paid, Viscera Seer sacrificed. Target chosen: Gravecrawler.
Bastion of Remembrance's triggered ability — 'Whenever a creature you control dies, each opponent loses 1 life and you gain 1 life.' Triggered on Viscera Seer's death during cost payment.

Undying triggered ability granted to Viscera Seer by Mikaeus, the Unhallowed — 'When a creature with undying dies, if it had no +1/+1 counters on it, return it to the battlefield under its owner's control with a +1/+1 counter on it.' Triggered on Viscera Seer's death during cost payment.

extras.pod_size: Five players — you and four opponents, 160 opposing life in total (opponent life is on the board block). Your 39 is 40 less the 1 life already paid for the ability on the stack.
extras.library: You have 60 cards in your library.
assumptions: No player responds to anything; every opponent passes priority throughout.
No permanent enters or leaves the battlefield except as described by the cards named here.
It is your precombat main phase.
Nest of Scarabs is NOT on the battlefield, so no Insect tokens are created by anything here.
Viscera Seer is a Vampire Wizard and Gravecrawler is a Zombie — both are non-Human, so Mikaeus grants both +1/+1 and undying.
extras.note_for_the_resolver: This deck's declared SECOND KILL is built on Mikaeus, and Mikaeus carries more contained combo lines than any other card in the 99 — nineteen. None has ever been resolved. The board is deliberately minimal: two non-Human bodies, the commander, a drain that cannot be eaten, and no Nest of Scarabs. The crux is what happens to Gravecrawler's counters when the ability resolves.

scenario.question: Resolve the stack. When Yawgmoth's ability puts a -1/-1 counter on Gravecrawler, which already carries a +1/+1 counter, what does the next state-based-action check do to those counters — and is Gravecrawler afterwards eligible for undying the next time it dies? Then state what bounds repetition of this loop.

steps.action: No player responds; priority passes and the stack resolves top-down (last in, first out). The topmost object is pos 2, the undying triggered ability granted to Viscera Seer by Mikaeus. Below it sit pos 1 (Bastion of Remembrance's death trigger) and pos 0 (Yawgmoth's activated ability, both of whose costs — 1 life, sacrifice Viscera Seer — are already paid).
steps.effect: Resolution order is: undying trigger, then Bastion trigger, then Yawgmoth's ability. Viscera Seer is in the graveyard and is NOT a body on the battlefield; the board entering this resolution is three creatures — Yawgmoth 2/4, Mikaeus 5/5, Gravecrawler (2/1 printed, +1/+1 from Mikaeus, one +1/+1 counter = 4/3).

steps.action: The undying trigger resolves. Undying is a leaves-the-battlefield ability with an intervening 'if' clause: 'if it had no +1/+1 counters on it'. Viscera Seer is now a new object in the graveyard, so the condition is evaluated against the creature as it last existed ON THE BATTLEFIELD — where it had no counters at all (it was 1/1 printed, 2/2 only because of Mikaeus's static +1/+1, which is not a counter).
steps.effect: The condition is true both at trigger time and again on resolution, so the ability resolves: Viscera Seer returns to the battlefield under its owner's control with a +1/+1 counter on it. It returns as a new object with no memory of its previous existence.

steps.effect: YES — Gravecrawler is eligible for undying the next time it dies. It now has no +1/+1 counters, so if it is sacrificed in this state the condition is true both when the trigger would go on the stack and again on resolution, and it returns with a fresh +1/+1 counter. Symmetrically, Viscera Seer is currently NOT eligible: it carries the +1/+1 counter from step 2 until something removes it. Exactly one of the two non-Human bodies is armed at any time, and Yawgmoth's -1/-1 counter is what flips which one.

steps.action: THE SWAP, VERIFIED ON THE OTHER BODY. Each further iteration is one activation of Yawgmoth: pay 1 life, sacrifice the body that currently carries NO +1/+1 counter (it returns via undying with one), and put the -1/-1 counter on the OTHER body. On the very first swap that other body is VISCERA SEER, which is printed 1/1 — smaller than Gravecrawler — so the step-6 state-based-action check must be re-performed for it rather than assumed. At that check Viscera Seer is 1/1 printed, +1/+1 from Mikaeus, one +1/+1 counter and one -1/-1 counter, all in layer 7c: power 1+1+1-1 = 2, toughness 1+1+1-1 = 2.
steps.effect: Toughness is 2, not 0 or less, so the creature-death state-based action does NOT apply to Viscera Seer and it survives the check. In that same single state-based-action event established in step 6, N = 1 counter of each kind is removed, leaving Viscera Seer a 2/2 with ZERO counters — re-armed for undying exactly as Gravecrawler was in step 6, while Gravecrawler now carries the +1/+1 counter from its own undying return. The alternation therefore holds in both directions: the pair swaps roles every activation, and neither body ever dies to the counter itself.

steps.action: WHAT BOUNDS REPETITION, AND THE ONE TRAP ON THIS BOARD. First, that the line repeats at all: after step 6's state-based-action check the stack is empty, it is your precombat main phase and priority returns to you, and a player may activate an activated ability any time they have priority. Yawgmoth's ability carries no mana symbol in its cost and no activation restriction, so it may be activated again at {0} available — that is what makes steps 8-10 repetition claims rather than a one-shot. Three quantities then bound the repetition, and the one further free sacrifice outlet on this board is a TRAP, not a bonus.
steps.effect: (1) LIFE is not the bound: you pay 1 life per activation and Bastion returns exactly 1 life per creature death, so your total is flat at 40 and the 119.4 requirement that you have at least the life you are paying is never threatened. (2) DRAIN is the clock: one creature dies per activation, so each activation removes 1 life PER OPPONENT and 4 across the pod. From the post-resolution 39 per seat, 39 further activations put every opponent at 0 and they lose to state-based actions; that is 156 pod life removed. (3) The LIBRARY is the hard bound and it is finite: Yawgmoth's ability reads 'Put a -1/-1 counter on up to one target creature and draw a card' with no 'may', and its controller follows those instructions in the order written, so the draw is MANDATORY and cannot be declined. With 59 cards left you may activate at most 59 more times; a 60th activation would attempt a draw from an empty library and YOU lose the game at the next state-based-action check. The loop is therefore NOT infinite — a 59-activation engine that needs 39, with 20 activations of margin. (4) THE SECOND OUTLET IS A TRAP — CORRECTED FROM THE PREVIOUS PASS, WHICH CALLED IT 'STRICTLY FAVOURABLE'. Viscera Seer is back on the battlefield from step 2 and has its own activated ability, 'Sacrifice a creature: Scry 1' — an activated ability written cost-then-effect whose cost contains no mana symbol, so it is free even at {0} available, and each use kills a creature and so triggers Bastion for another 1 per seat while consuming no library. READ THE COST EXACTLY, BECAUSE THE PREVIOUS PASS DID NOT: the Seer's cost is 'Sacrifice A creature', NOT 'another creature' as Yawgmoth's cost is. The Seer may therefore eat ANY creature you control — including Mikaeus, including Yawgmoth, and including ITSELF. That distinction is what makes the finisher count 5 rather than 3. It is nevertheless ENGINE-ENDING if used mid-loop, and a pilot who reads 'free extra drain' and fires it kills their own combo. WHY: the engine's steady state is exactly one ARMED body (no +1/+1 counter, undying-eligible) and one LOADED body (one +1/+1 counter, not eligible), and only Yawgmoth's -1/-1 counter can strip a +1/+1 counter — it does so via the step-6 state-based action, one counter per activation, which is why one Yawgmoth activation re-arms exactly one body. The Seer's ability places no counter at all. So if you sacrifice the ARMED body to the Seer, undying returns it WITH a +1/+1 counter and now BOTH bodies are loaded and NEITHER is undying-eligible; and if you sacrifice the LOADED body to the Seer, its undying trigger's intervening 'if' is false and that body is gone PERMANENTLY. THE TWO BRANCHES DIFFER IN WHERE THE PERMANENT LOSS FALLS, AND THE PREVIOUS PASS'S 'either way the next Yawgmoth activation must sacrifice a counter-bearing body' IS FALSE IN THE SECOND: in branch A (armed body eaten) nothing is lost yet, both bodies carry counters, and the NEXT Yawgmoth activation must sacrifice a counter-bearing body, which dies for good; in branch B (loaded body eaten) the permanent loss has ALREADY happened and the survivor is ARMED, so the next Yawgmoth sacrifice loses nothing permanently — it returns loaded. THE CONCLUSION IS UNCHANGED, because both branches converge on the same state, ONE alternation body, and one body can never sustain the alternation. An activation kills exactly one body and yields exactly one -1/-1 counter, which strips exactly one +1/+1 counter, and it can never strip the counter on the body it just ate: that body was sacrificed to pay the cost, so if you had targeted it, on resolution it is no longer in the zone it was in when it was targeted and is an illegal target; and if you targeted anything else, its +1/+1 counter simply stays. Re-arming therefore always costs a DIFFERENT body's death, and with one alternation body left the only other creatures are Mikaeus — whose death removes undying from that body entirely, since the grant is his — and Yawgmoth, which its own 'another creature' cost may not sacrifice. The alternation is over within one or two further activations in both branches. ONE mid-loop Seer sacrifice therefore buys 1 drain per seat and costs you roughly 34 of the 39 activations you still need: you collect about five drains from the collapsing board instead of the 39 the intact alternation would have delivered. THE ONLY SAFE USE IS AS A FINISHER, after the alternation is no longer needed — and at that point at most FIVE free Seer sacrifices exist in total, CORRECTED FROM THREE, which omitted Mikaeus and Yawgmoth. The finisher board is exactly four bodies: Yawgmoth, Mikaeus, and the two alternation bodies, one armed and one loaded, one of which is the Seer itself. Order it so the SEER EATS ITSELF LAST, since its outlet leaves the battlefield with it: (1) sacrifice the ARMED body — it dies for a Bastion drain and undying returns it LOADED, no permanent loss; (2)-(4) sacrifice, in any order, the three bodies other than the Seer that are now on the battlefield — the loaded alternation body (its intervening 'if' is false, permanent), Mikaeus (his own grant reads 'OTHER non-Human creatures you control get +1/+1 and have undying', so it excludes himself and he has no undying, permanent) and Yawgmoth (a Legendary Creature — Human Cleric per cards.json, so Mikaeus's non-Human grant never reached it, permanent); (5) sacrifice the Seer to itself, permanent. Five deaths, five Bastion drains, zero library consumed. The count is the same 5 in EITHER orientation of which alternation body is armed: if the Seer is the armed body, it is step (1) and it comes straight back to keep working. SIX IS IMPOSSIBLE: four bodies plus exactly ONE undying return, because only one body is armed at a time and neither Yawgmoth (Human) nor Mikaeus (excluded by his own 'Other') can undy. ACCOUNTING CONSEQUENCE: margin = 59 - (39 - k) = 20 + k, where k is the number of finisher Seer sacrifices taken and 0 <= k <= 5. The margin is 20 activations clean and at most 25 with all five finisher sacrifices — a bounded range, NOT an open-ended lower bound as an earlier pass asserted, and NOT the 20-23 the previous pass computed from a count of three. Nothing else on this board caps the loop: the loop costs no mana, Gravecrawler cannot be recast from the graveyard because that requires {B} and mana available is {0}, and Mikaeus need only remain on the battlefield, which it does because Yawgmoth's cost sacrifices 'another creature' and you always choose one of the two designated bodies.

steps.action: HOW THE KILL BECOMES A WIN. The 39th further activation brings every opponent from 1 to 0 life; the drain is one simultaneous event per Bastion resolution, so all four seats reach 0 together and all four lose the game at the next state-based-action check. You are still in the game at that moment: your life is flat at 40 (step 9, item 1), and you have used 39 of the 59 draws the library permits, so the deck-out state-based action has not been met.
steps.effect: With all four of your opponents having left the game and you still in it, you win the game immediately. This is the rule that converts four simultaneous losses in a five-player pod into a win; the loss of the opponents alone does not state it. The Mikaeus + Yawgmoth line is a verified kill on this board.

citations.quote: A player still in the game wins the game if that player’s opponents have all left the game. This happens immediately and overrides all effects that would preclude that player from winning the game.

final_state.summary: The stack fully resolves. Undying returns Viscera Seer (its condition read off the creature as it last existed on the battlefield, where it had no counters) with a +1/+1 counter, so it is 3/3. Bastion drains 1 life PER OPPONENT (4 seats x 1 = 4 across the pod, 160 -> 156) and gains you 1, putting you back to 40. Yawgmoth's ability then resolves on its still-legal target: Gravecrawler takes a -1/-1 counter and you draw. THE CRUX: the next state-based-action check removes one +1/+1 and one -1/-1 counter from Gravecrawler simultaneously (704.5q), leaving it with ZERO counters at 3/2 and alive — so YES, Gravecrawler is eligible for undying the next time it dies. The -1/-1 counter is not a shrink, it is a RESET. The same check is verified on the other body: Viscera Seer, printed 1/1, is 2/2 when it holds both counters, so toughness 2 clears 704.5f and it survives to be re-armed in its turn — the alternation holds in both directions. Repetition is legal: priority returns to you with the stack empty and a player may activate an activated ability any time they have priority (117.1b), and the ability needs no mana. The loop is FINITE: life is flat (pay 1, Bastion returns 1), the drain clock needs 39 more activations to zero all four opponents, and the draw is mandatory (608.2c — no 'may' on the card), capping the engine at 59 more activations before you deck yourself. THE TRAP, corrected from the previous pass: Viscera Seer's own free 'Sacrifice a creature: Scry 1' outlet is NOT a strictly favourable bonus. It places no counter, and only Yawgmoth's -1/-1 counter can strip the +1/+1 counter an undying return leaves behind, one per activation — so a mid-loop Seer sacrifice either loads BOTH bodies (sac the armed one; 702.93a returns it with a counter) or permanently loses one (sac the loaded one; undying's intervening 'if' fails). The two branches differ in WHERE the permanent loss falls, and the previous pass's 'either way' sentence was wrong about it: in branch A (armed body eaten) nothing is lost yet and the NEXT Yawgmoth sacrifice is the one that loses a body for good; in branch B (loaded body eaten) the loss has ALREADY happened and the survivor is armed, so the next Yawgmoth sacrifice loses nothing permanently. The conclusion is unchanged because both branches converge on ONE alternation body, and one body can never be re-armed: an activation's single -1/-1 counter can never land on the body that same activation sacrificed to pay its cost — that body is no longer in the zone it was in when it was targeted, so it is an illegal target (608.2b) — and re-arming therefore always costs a different body's death, which with one body left means eating Mikaeus (who is the source of undying) or nothing. Fire the Seer mid-loop and you trade 1 drain per seat for roughly 34 of the 39 activations you need. Use it ONLY as a finisher, where at most FIVE such sacrifices exist — CORRECTED from three: the Seer's cost is 'Sacrifice a creature', NOT 'another creature', so it also eats Mikaeus (whose 'Other non-Human' grant excludes himself) and Yawgmoth (a Human Cleric, whom that grant never reached), and finally itself; four bodies plus the one available undying return is 5, and six is impossible. Margin is therefore 20 activations clean and at most 25 with all five finisher sacrifices — a bounded range, not an open lower bound. All four opponents reach 0 together and leave the game; you are still in it, so you win (104.2a). VERDICT on the deck's declared second kill: the Mikaeus + Yawgmoth line is REAL and lethal on this board, but it is a library-bounded loop, not an infinite combo. A containment record is not a verification; this resolves one of the nineteen and it holds with 20 activations of margin (20-25 depending on finisher Seer sacrifices).

Viscera Seer (3/3 — 1/1 printed, one +1/+1 counter, +1/+1 from Mikaeus; undying NOT available while that counter remains — this is the LOADED body; its own free sacrifice outlet is live but is a TRAP mid-loop, see step 9 item 4; at most FIVE free Seer sacrifices exist as a finisher)

drain_accounting.margin_note: 20 further activations of margin (59 library-permitted minus 39 needed) is the working figure and it assumes Viscera Seer's free sacrifice outlet is NEVER used mid-loop: a mid-loop Seer sacrifice either loads both bodies (branch A, and the NEXT Yawgmoth sacrifice is then the permanent loss) or immediately loses the body it ate (branch B, after which the survivor is armed and the next Yawgmoth sacrifice loses nothing). Both branches converge on one alternation body, which can never be re-armed, so the engine ends either way. Used only as a finisher, at most FIVE Seer sacrifices exist — the Seer's cost is 'Sacrifice a creature', not 'another creature', so it eats Mikaeus and Yawgmoth as well as the two alternation bodies, and exactly one undying return is available — and each substitutes for one Yawgmoth activation, so margin = 20 + k for 0 <= k <= 5, i.e. 20-25. It is NOT an open-ended lower bound.

margin_range.note: Seer sacrifices are safe only after the alternation is no longer needed. The maximum of 5 = four bodies at the finisher board (Yawgmoth, Mikaeus, and the two alternation bodies) plus the single available undying return; Yawgmoth is a Human and Mikaeus's grant reads 'Other', so neither of them undies. Six is impossible.
